ei.title: 2번: A Heart Syndrome Caused by Extreme Emotions
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: Broken heart syndrome, also known as takotsubo syndrome (TTS), is a condition that occurs when stress weakens the heart's ability to pump blood. TTS can occur after stressful events such as the loss of a family member or a natural disaster. Surprisingly, researchers say people can also get TTS when happy things occur, sometimes referring to this as "happy heart syndrome." A researcher discovered this while analyzing data from 1,750 patients with takotsubo syndrome. Of the 485 patients diagnosed after emotional events, 20 had experienced happy events. The researcher concluded that the brain reacts similarly to extremely positive and negative events, so both can result in takotsubo syndrome.

questions.passage: Broken heart syndrome, also known as takotsubo syndrome (TTS), is a condition that occurs when stress (A)[strengthens / weakens] the heart's ability to pump blood. TTS can occur after (B)[stressful / pleasant] events such as the loss of a family member or a natural disaster. (C)[Predictably / Surprisingly], researchers say people can also get TTS when happy things occur, sometimes referring to this as "happy heart syndrome." A researcher discovered this while analyzing data from 1,750 patients with takotsubo syndrome. Of the 485 patients diagnosed after emotional events, 20 had experienced happy events. The researcher concluded that the brain reacts similarly to extremely positive and negative events, so both can result in takotsubo syndrome.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) weakens=약화시키다 / strengthens=강화하다 (B) stressful=스트레스가 많은 / pleasant=즐거운 (C) Surprisingly=놀랍게도 / Predictably=예상대로
det.analysis:
① weakens — stressful — Surprisingly: 스트레스가 심장 기능을 '약화시키고', '스트레스가 많은' 사건 뒤에 발생하며, 행복한 일에도 생긴다니 '놀랍게도'가 자연스럽다 ←정답
② strengthens/Predictably: 심장을 '강화한다'는 반대, '예상대로'도 놀라움 표현과 반대
③ pleasant/Predictably: '즐거운 사건(상실·자연재해)'은 문맥과 반대
④ strengthens/pleasant: 둘 다 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 스트레스가 심장을 weakens(약화), stressful(스트레스성) 사건, 행복에도 생겨서 Surprisingly(놀랍게도)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) concluded=결론지었다 / doubted=의심했다 (B) similarly=비슷하게 / differently=다르게 (C) result in=~을 초래하다 / prevent=막다
det.analysis:
① doubted: 연구자가 '의심했다'? 데이터로 밝혔으므로 concluded(결론지었다)가 맞음
② concluded — similarly — result in: 뇌가 긍정·부정 사건에 '비슷하게' 반응해 둘 다 병을 '초래한다'고 '결론지었다' ←정답
③ differently/prevent: '다르게' 반응하는데 둘 다 초래한다는 모순, prevent(막다)도 반대
④ doubted/differently: 둘 다 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 연구자가 concluded(결론), 뇌가 similarly(비슷하게) 반응, 둘 다 result in(초래)

det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 condition의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

③ (A) 상태 (B) 질환: (B)에서 취업의 '질환'? 부적절

det.analysis: analyze를 -ing 형태 analyzing으로 변환. 'while analyzing data' = '데이터를 분석하는 동안/분석하면서' — 접속사 while 뒤에서 동시동작을 나타내는 분사(V-ing)가 필요해요.
det.tip: while _____ = ~하면서 → 분사(V-ing) → analyzing

questions.passage: The researcher concluded that the brain __________ (react) similarly to extremely positive and negative events.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: react(동사: 반응하다) → reacts(3인칭 단수 현재형). 주어 the brain이 단수
det.analysis: react를 reacts로 변환. 주어 'the brain(뇌)'은 3인칭 단수이고 현재의 일반적 사실을 말하므로 동사에 -s를 붙여요. 'the brain reacts' = '뇌가 반응한다'.
det.tip: 주어 the brain(3인칭 단수) + 현재 → 동사에 -s → reacts

questions.passage: Broken heart syndrome, also known as takotsubo syndrome (TTS), is a condition that occurs when stress weakens the heart's ability to pump blood. TTS can occur after stressful events such as the loss of a family member or a __________. Surprisingly, researchers say people can also get TTS when happy things occur, sometimes referring to this as "happy heart syndrome." A researcher discovered this while analyzing data from 1,750 patients with takotsubo syndrome. Of the 485 patients diagnosed after emotional events, 20 had experienced happy events. The researcher concluded that the brain reacts similarly to extremely positive and negative events, so both can result in takotsubo syndrome.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: birthday party=생일 파티 / job promotion=승진 / natural disaster=자연재해 / happy memory=행복한 기억
det.analysis:
① birthday party: 생일 파티 — 스트레스성 사건이 아닌 즐거운 일
② job promotion: 승진 — 긍정적 사건
③ natural disaster: 가족의 상실과 함께 나열되는 스트레스성 사건 = 자연재해 ←정답
④ happy memory: 행복한 기억 — 스트레스성과 반대
det.tip: the loss of a family member or a _____ = 상실과 나란한 스트레스성 사건 = natural disaster

questions.passage: Broken heart syndrome, also known as takotsubo syndrome (TTS), is a condition that occurs when stress weakens the heart's ability to pump blood. TTS can occur after stressful events such as the loss of a family member or a natural disaster. Surprisingly, researchers say people can also get TTS when happy things occur, sometimes referring to this as "happy heart syndrome." A researcher discovered this while analyzing data from 1,750 patients with takotsubo syndrome. Of the 485 patients diagnosed after emotional events, 20 had experienced happy events. The researcher concluded that the brain reacts similarly to extremely positive and negative events, so both can __________ takotsubo syndrome.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: result in=~을 초래하다 / result from=~에서 비롯되다 / protect against=~로부터 보호하다 / recover from=~에서 회복하다
det.analysis:
① result in: 극도의 긍정·부정 사건이 '둘 다' takotsubo syndrome을 초래할 수 있다 ←정답
② result from: '~에서 비롯되다'는 인과 방향이 반대 (사건이 원인이므로 result in)
③ protect against: '보호한다'는 병을 유발한다는 문맥과 반대
④ recover from: '회복한다'도 문맥과 반대
det.tip: both can _____ takotsubo syndrome = 둘 다 병을 result in(초래)
